question: For each issued, nonvoid invoice outstanding on 2026-03-31, return its ID and positive balance in cents as of that date.
sql:
SELECT i.id,
       SUM(l.amount_cents)
         - COALESCE((SELECT SUM(pa.amount_cents)
                     FROM payment_allocations pa
                     JOIN payments p ON p.id = pa.payment_id
                     WHERE pa.invoice_id = i.id
                       AND p.status = 'succeeded'
                       AND pa.allocated_on <= '2026-03-31'), 0)
         - COALESCE((SELECT SUM(ca.amount_cents)
                     FROM credit_applications ca
                     WHERE ca.invoice_id = i.id
                       AND ca.applied_on <= '2026-03-31'), 0) AS balance_cents
FROM invoices i
JOIN invoice_lines l ON l.invoice_id = i.id
WHERE i.status = 'issued' AND i.issued_on <= '2026-03-31'
GROUP BY i.id
HAVING balance_cents > 0
ORDER BY i.id;
wrong_sql:
SELECT i.id,
       SUM(l.amount_cents)
         - COALESCE((SELECT SUM(pa.amount_cents)
                     FROM payment_allocations pa
                     JOIN payments p ON p.id = pa.payment_id
                     WHERE pa.invoice_id = i.id
                       AND p.status = 'succeeded'
                       AND pa.allocated_on <= '2026-03-31'), 0)
         - COALESCE((SELECT SUM(ca.amount_cents)
                     FROM credit_applications ca
                     WHERE ca.invoice_id = i.id
                       AND ca.applied_on <= '2026-03-31'), 0) AS balance_cents
FROM invoices i
JOIN invoice_lines l ON l.invoice_id = i.id
WHERE i.issued_on <= '2026-03-31'
GROUP BY i.id
HAVING balance_cents > 0
ORDER BY i.id;
witness: Invoice 6 is status 'void' (lines 9000 cents) with credit application 1500 cents applied on 2026-03-16; dropping the status = 'issued' filter adds row [6, 7500] to the result. All other rows are identical, so this fixture fact isolates the void-exclusion assumption. Balances: inv1 6500-3000=3500 (alloc 8 on 2026-04-15 excluded), inv2 3000-1800-1000=200 (credit appl 2 on 2026-03-28), inv3 8000-3000-800=4200 (alloc 3 boundary 2026-03-31 included), inv4 2500 (alloc 4 on 2026-04-10 excluded), inv5 6000-2000-1000=3000 (alloc 6 on 2026-04-05 excluded, credit appl 4 boundary 2026-03-31 included), inv7 4500 (alloc 7 on 2026-04-05 excluded), inv8 1200 (credit appl 3 on 2026-04-05 excluded).

question: Which payment IDs were successfully allocated to at least two distinct invoices by 2026-03-31?
sql:
SELECT pa.payment_id
FROM payment_allocations pa
JOIN payments p ON p.id = pa.payment_id
WHERE p.status = 'succeeded' AND pa.allocated_on <= '2026-03-31'
GROUP BY pa.payment_id
HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT pa.invoice_id) >= 2
ORDER BY pa.payment_id;
wrong_sql:
SELECT pa.payment_id
FROM payment_allocations pa
JOIN payments p ON p.id = pa.payment_id
WHERE p.status = 'succeeded'
GROUP BY pa.payment_id
HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT pa.invoice_id) >= 2
ORDER BY pa.payment_id;
witness: Payment 105 (succeeded, received 2026-04-05) was allocated to invoice 5 (3000 cents) and invoice 7 (1000 cents), both on 2026-04-05, which is after the 2026-03-31 cutoff; dropping the allocated_on cutoff adds row [105]. Payment 101 was allocated to invoices 1 and 2 on 2026-03-25 (within cutoff) and is the only correct answer. Failed payment 106 has no allocations, so it cannot mask this error.
